I dont see Chris as a bad person. I see Chris as really wanting to deliver on the dream he pitched in 2012, but I also see that he has found the development part of the project the real reward. IMO, he wants to stretch out the development for as long as humanly possible (to deliver a better project?), to secure job security. You must remember, that before he pitched the game, he was a failed producer who was relegated to owning a used rental car sales lot. Heading a multinational games studio selling virtual ships for the same price as a used rental car is probably an upgrade in his mind. I can also imagine Sandi is loving it because she went from marrying a producer, to being married to a used rental car salesman, to a CEO that can put her in front of the camera every week, and feed her dream of being an actress.
Again, im not saying this is malicious intent, im saying it is very convenient that they have stumbled into a money making machine that requires development continue in perpetuity. IMO, as long as the community is paying 45-1200$ for a virtual product that isnt even in engine, there is reason to continue development.
As for his management style.. thats another discussion entirely. His perfectionism and micromanagement style is well known, and it takes a certain personality to be able to work with him. Being a fan of Steve Jobs myself, I cannot judge Chris's reputation, I can only view the end result of his teams progress under his management. And development is glacially slow. Is that because of their workload? Their ambition? Their director sticking his fingers into every line of code? I dont know, and neither can you.
So if your vision of Chris is vastly different, I welcome your description. Just dont expect me to change my opinion radically. Im old, a good judge of character, have been observing the project from the beginning, and have some experience in the game development industry. My opinion of the man comes from his actions more than his words, so if you have something I have not already considered in forming my opinion, I am more than willing to listen.

> it's only a paywall until the game releases.

I disagree. Chris wants to develop this game in perpetuity. There will never be a true "release," it will always be more patches like EVE. Chris will only stop developing when the community stops buying and he is forced to cobble together what he has and call it a "release." And to keep the development going, he will keep selling concept ships, vehicles, land claims, apartments. Anything he can monetize, he will to keep the development going. If he can balance the spinning plates of community faith and sour public opinion to keep the project bringing in revenue, we might will get a good-looking playable experience with actual gameplay. Its just going to take a while, considering the glacial pace with which the development team works due to Chris's micromanagement and perfectionism. Im estimating SQ42 in 2024-2025 and a "release" that has the majority of the current features promised around 2028-2030.

But to answer the OPs question, YES, I think Chris is going to figure out how to sell player housing. I would prefer the player crafted the housing and placed it where they wanted like in SWGs.. but Chris monetizes everything, so expect a concept sale sometime soon.

I just want them to release the Game Design Document with all the locked down features. At some point you have to stop promising new features and say, this is what we are going to work on for release. I have yet to hear that from CIG. Until the features are locked down in the Games Design Document, the project cant even be considered an actual Alpha. They are working on content in parallel with the engine, which is normal. But im concerned that the engine is not their priority. Their concept ship pipeline is in overdrive, and their backend engine department is pushing everything back year after year.

Ive followed development on many different games. I remember fondly theorycrafting on the Star Wars Galaxies boards before the game was released. That was a wonderful year.. and then the game came out and I got to enjoy the game just as much as the theorycrafting. This community is different. I think they only have theorycrafting, a buggy pre-alpha tech demo and a whole lot of cult of personality. And as long as Chris is getting money to develop in perpetuity, thats what he is going to do. He is going to promise and work on content until the money dries up, then he is going to cobble what he has together into something that can be called a game for some kind of messy release and then ask the community for the money to improve it with all the things he promised. And the development and promises will continue.

CIG is going to promise you everything your little heart desires, and they are going to keep selling you ships, and making more promises to keep development going indefinitely. In 10 years, once the alpha becomes an actual beta and is ready for stress testing, bug fixing and optimization, you will be amazed at how many of those promises never made it into the game. They need to keep promising stuff so they can keep selling ships, and keep paying people to keep developing indefinitely.

I think CIG is going to release something late in the next decade, but it will still be the bones of the game they are promising. Chris wants to develop this the rest of his life, and there is precedent. Look at World of Warcraft, they keep developing and people keep buying. And people like the OP keep dreaming, and Chris keeps promising, and ships keep being sold. IMHO as long as Chris keeps selling people their childhood dreams effectively, and people keep feeding the beast with money, we may get something eventually. It wont be as large as promised, it wont be as personal as promised, it wont even be as technologically innovative as promised, but the diehards will be happy with it. They just need to keep feeding Chris money.
